issuer_id.description: Exact issuing actor. Its closed ActorId shape already contains the account routing authority when one exists; no parallel station sidecar is permitted.

items.description: Canonical action vocabulary. MUST be of the form ak.<segment>.<segment>... matching capabilities.md §5. Bare names without the ak. prefix are not permitted; consult capabilities.md before introducing new action names. Wildcards within a segment are not permitted in this schema; the resource selector controls scope, not action expansion.

constraints.description: Constraints applied to this grant. Re-grant control MUST be expressed via constraint_kind='authority_control' and max_authority_depth (see capabilities.md §10). A top-level 'delegable' field is forbidden and MUST be rejected as schema_violation. With no authority_control constraint the grant cannot be re-granted (equivalent to max_authority_depth=0).

issued_at.description: Grant issuance time — carries the 'creation time' semantics for a Capability Grant in place of the generic created_at (models/common-fields.md §3.2). Retention / audit / ordering queries MUST use issued_at / expires_at / revoked_at rather than falling back to created_at.

updated_by.description: Reducer-derived actor that produced the most recent grant lifecycle update. Ordinary grant body fields remain immutable; revocation still uses revoked_by/revoked_at.

updated_at.description: Reducer-derived timestamp for the most recent grant lifecycle update. Ordinary grant body fields remain immutable; revocation still uses revoked_by/revoked_at.

issuer_authority_refs.description: The committed authority this grant was issued under. A root controller's grant anchors on the accepted Realm authority Event; any further grant anchors on grants its issuer already holds. Authorization is recomputed from these refs on every decision, so revoking an ancestor invalidates its descendants without a cascading write.

oneOf.description: A grant the issuer holds. The issuer MUST be that grant's subject, and the ref MUST be active at evaluation time; its capability, resources and constraints all bound this child.

authority_event_ref.description: The accepted Realm genesis or owner-transfer Event that established the issuing controller.

authority_generation.description: The governance Station generation at issuance. It is checked against the committed authority history rather than a mutable typed current result.

oneOf.description: A committed Realm authority root. It is terminal for cycle checks. realm_id is explicit because ak.capability.derived can carry roots from another Realm.

authority_depth.description: Reducer-derived absolute distance from the authority root: a realm_root ref counts 0, so a root controller's grant is 1 and a member's re-grant is 2. Derived from the refs, never author-declared, so it cannot be misreported — which is what makes it safe to answer 'how far did this authority spread' with a single field instead of a recursive join. Taken at issuance and not recomputed on revocation; a later chain may be shorter than the recorded value, which is the conservative direction for a max_authority_depth decision.

authority_root_refs.description: Reducer-derived set of committed authority roots this grant ultimately descends from: direct realm_root refs plus the union of every parent grant's roots. Deduplicated on (realm_id, authority_event_ref, authority_generation) and sorted canonically by unsigned-byte order.

allOf.$comment: Lint condition (2) from capabilities.md §18.1: grants whose actions[] include moderator-role actions MUST carry a constraint with depends_on_moderation_state=true. Conditions (1) and (3) (subject condition selector referencing moderation state, constraints referencing moderation queue/typed current result) are reducer-side lint and not enforced here.
